The pion and the electron belong to diff.why: Texts give each particle's family on its own (the pion is a meson, the electron a lepton); nobody states whether two particles share a family, so the model combines two separate facts. The direct forms are absent.

notes: The earlier audit showed this edit is held (the pion is a meson for all four models); what failed was wording, so the fill-in-the-blank questions ('a meson or a lepton?') are rephrased as plain 'which family' questions and the earlier 'unlikely' rating is dropped for the stored one. in_particle_family is functional, so the old family drops out in every world (near, far); the two same-family derived queries compare the pion's new family with the electron's and the muon's, so no stored pion property (such as being a boson) can compete with them. The indeterminate query is a background-belief case about the size of the lepton family. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama).
